messages:
bryan: Hey team — noticed a spike in 5xx/429s and token usage after we upgraded to redwood-python 2.0.0 yesterday. Rolling back to 1.38 drops errors. Any idea what's changed?

support-bot: Thanks @bryan — can you paste the SDK version + a minimal repro (code snippet and any relevant headers/log lines)? :mag:

bryan: We're on 2.0.0 (pip). Minimal sync snippet:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=..., timeout=30)
resp = client.generate(prompt="hello")
```
Behavior: requests block >60s sometimes, client retries kick in and we observe duplicate completions + higher token counts. Logs show repeated requests with same payload but no Idempotency-Key.

maria: Do you set an Idempotency-Key? Also which retry config? Note: v2 shipped some defaults changes.

bryan: We didn't set an Idempotency-Key explicitly. No custom retry config. Just using default client.

jess: Investigating — quick summary from eng: in 2.0.0 we renamed the per-call param `timeout` -> `request_timeout` to disambiguate from internal timers. Unfortunately the sync client path accidentally ignored the old `timeout` name (no deprecation warning), so user-provided `timeout` was silently dropped. Separately the retry defaults were widened to retry on 5xx for non-idempotent endpoints. That combination can cause the client to wait the server default, then retry, which looks like stacked duplicate calls and higher token consumption.

ryan-eng: Repro steps we used: 1) pip install redwood==2.0.0 2) run the snippet with `timeout=10` 3) force server 502 for the first call -> client retries with same body and no idempotency header -> two billable completions.

bryan: Ouch. What's the recommended immediate workaround? Pinning?

maria: Short term: pin to the last 1.x patch: `pip install redwood==1.38.4` or explicitly pass the new arg: `request_timeout=30` and set retries low: `retries={"max_attempts": 1}`. Also add an Idempotency-Key header for requests that create billable side effects.

jess: Example workaround: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="...", request_timeout=30, retries={"max_attempts": 1})
resp = client.generate(prompt="hello", headers={"Idempotency-Key": "{{your-unique-key}}"})
```
This forces the client to not attempt multiple attempts and uses the new, supported param name.

bryan: Can billing team help reconcile the extra tokens? We saw a ~12% bump for our org during the window.

ryan-eng: We'll open a billing ticket and correlate request ids. @billing-team (not in thread) — we'll pass request traces. We'll likely issue credits for obvious duplicates caused by this regression.

jess: Patch plan: we will ship 2.0.1 with two things: 1) restore compatibility (honor `timeout` again with a deprecation warning) 2) revert retry default for non-idempotent generation to previous behavior. Patch scheduled for 15:00 PT today. Release notes + advisory will go out on the changelog and we'll post here when live. :white_check_mark:

bryan: Thanks — pinned to 1.38 for now and applying the workaround. Please @me when the patch is out.

maria: Noted. We'll follow up with a clear migration note and a short snippet for migration (timeout -> request_timeout, plus idempotency guidance) so other customers don't hit this.

jess: Also adding a small integration test to catch this for future releases. Thanks for the quick report, @bryan. :raised_hands:
